title: Space bound for compiled register programs
statement: Let $A$ be a register program with $m$ registers and access to $d$ Boolean oracles, let $x$ be a Boolean input, and let $D$ be a $k_D$-work-tape machine with designated initial states $q_0(j)$ for each oracle. Suppose the run of $A$ from its initial state, zeroed registers, and no stored answer halts after $N$ steps with answer $b$. Suppose also that at every time $t<N$, its configuration satisfies the precondition for $A$, and every register value $v(r)$ satisfies $\lvert\mathrm{bits}(v(r)+1)\rvert\le W$. Then the compiled machine halts on $x$ with output $b$ at some time, and its total space use is at most $m(W+2)+k_D(2B+1)$.
hypotheses_covered: A has finitely many states with decidable equality
D has finitely many states with decidable equality
The abstract run from the initial state and zeroed registers halts after N steps
The answer stored at time N is some Boolean b
At each time t < N, the configuration satisfies Pre(A, oracle, D, q0, B, x)
At each time t < N, every register r satisfies the stated bit-length bound by W
